chapter_title: Exploring Substances: Acidic, Basic, and Neutral
core_summary: Substances are classified into acidic, basic, or neutral based on their chemical behavior. Acidic substances taste sour and turn blue litmus paper red. Basic substances taste bitter, feel soapy to touch, and turn red litmus paper blue. Neutral substances show no color change on either red or blue litmus paper. Indicators are chemical dyes (natural or synthetic) that display distinct colors in acidic, basic, and neutral solutions.
key_concepts: To classify household liquid samples as acidic, basic, or neutral using litmus indicators.
To prepare and test a natural indicator solution from red rose petals.

key_terms.definition: A substance with a sour taste that turns blue litmus paper red.
A substance with a bitter taste, soapy feel, that turns red litmus paper blue.
A substance that exhibits distinct color changes when exposed to acidic or basic solutions.

key_takeaways: Acidic solutions also produce no color change on red litmus paper. You must test with blue litmus paper as well to confirm.
